examples.prompt: You are stuck in an endless cycle of whenever you die, you will resurrect as a different person in another world and the only way to break the cycle and return home is by destroying the world you are in. The problem? A prophesied hero or group of heroes always rise up to ruin your plans.
examples.response: I died a thousand times across a thousand worlds, only to rise again and shatter each realm to finally return home; yet every time I stood atop the crumbling throne of destruction, a new hero emerged from the ashes to stop me. In the latest iteration, I prepared to sever the fabric of reality with a single blow, but a child with a glowing sword appeared from the shadows. The prophecy had changed, for this time the hero was not alone, but a legion of them who knew my face and my name. My blade shattered against their united front, and the world did not end, but instead healed itself around my defeated form. I realized with a sinking heart that the only way to break the cycle was to accept my fate, for the heroes would never let me destroy another world.

examples.prompt: Tailor me a story of what it means to be human.
A new rule on Earth is made which allows everyone to legally kill 1 person in their life, this affects the world severely & changes how everybody acts.
examples.response: The moment the law was signed, the world held its breath as every citizen quietly identified their one permitted target; streets emptied not from fear but from a strange, collective relief that the weight of eternal guilt had finally been lifted. People began to walk with a new, terrifying clarity, scanning faces not for love or hate but for the single name they had chosen to erase; a grandmother wept as she handed her grandson a knife, whispering that he could take the life that had stolen his father's smile. In the weeks that followed, cities transformed into silent gardens where neighbors avoided eye contact, knowing that tomorrow might be the day their freedom arrived or their end came. The rule did not bring peace, but it did end the endless cycle of vengeance, leaving humanity to face the silence of a world where every life was now a choice.
